Step 3.5 sits between tag publication (Step 3) and GitHub Release publication (Steps 4–5), so any transient failure here — npm registry hiccup, tag propagation slower than the 5s sleep, or a concurrent merge to `main` making the `git push origin HEAD:main` a non-fast-forward — kills the job with the `vX.Y.Z` and `v1` tags already public but **no GitHub Release ever created**. A re-run doesn't repair it: Step 2 now sees the just-pushed tag as `LATEST_TAG`, finds no commits since it, sets `skip=true`, and the run goes green with Steps 4–5 skipped. The PR's risk section covers the tag being out, but not the release page being suppressed.

Fix: move this step after Step 5. `npx skills update` only needs the git tag, which Step 3 already pushed — release publication becomes immune to install/propagation failures, and a failure here still fails the workflow loudly as intended.

`npx --yes skills` executes whatever `skills@latest` resolves to at run time, and this job's checkout deliberately persists a push-to-`main` token (`AUTOMATION_GITHUB_TOKEN || GITHUB_TOKEN`) in `.git/config` — so a compromised or maliciously updated `skills` npm package gets code execution on the release runner with credentials that can rewrite the action code every consumer runs via `@v1`. This is the first executable `npx` in `.github/workflows/`, and the repo's own posture pins third-party supply chain elsewhere (SHA-pinned actions, `skills-lock.json` hashes).

Pin a concrete version (`npx --yes skills@X.Y.Z update ai-diff-reviewer`) and bump it deliberately, like any other dependency.

Once this lands, every self-review leg hard-fails on any PR whose branch doesn't contain `.review/extension.md`: the runtime reads the file unconditionally when the input is set (`scripts/reviewer.py:3667`) and a missing file hits the `OSError` path that flips the tracking comment to FAILED and returns exit 1. Long-lived branches cut before this merge — and fork PRs cut from older `main` — go red on **all** legs when `ready` is applied, blocking the gate with "Could not read prompt extension file" as the only signal.

Consider degrading a *missing* extension file to a logged warning + base-prompt-only review (split `except FileNotFoundError` from other `OSError`, which can stay fatal) — that matches the non-fatal treatment collapse-previous and the tracking comment already get, and stale branches still get reviewed.

`git diff --quiet` sees only tracked files, so a release that purely *adds* files under the skill (e.g. a new sub-skill directory) leaves this check green and prints a false "already at ${NEW_VERSION}; nothing to sync" while the new content is never committed. The lockfile hash and SKILL.md version bump usually change too and mask it, but the guard is one `git add -A` away from being airtight (the later directory-form `git add` on line 214 already stages new files — only the check misses them):

```suggestion
git add -A .agents/skills/ai-diff-reviewer skills-lock.json
if git diff --cached --quiet -- .agents/skills/ai-diff-reviewer skills-lock.json; then
```

This line duplicates line 358 verbatim ("**Option A — `.review/extension.md`** (recommended):" appears twice back-to-back). Since this vendored copy is a byte-copy of the released tag *and* of the `skills/ai-diff-reviewer/` source-of-truth, the fix belongs in `skills/ai-diff-reviewer/SKILL.md` (per the new DON'T #14 you'd never hand-edit this file) — worth doing in this PR or before the next tag so the Step 3.5 refresh cycle doesn't re-vendor the duplicate on every release.

```suggestion
**Option A — `.review/extension.md`** (recommended):
```

The citation is wrong on arity: `safe_repo_path` takes a single repo-relative path — `def safe_repo_path(rel: str) -> Path` (`scripts/reviewer.py:2122`) — not `(repo_root, candidate)`. This file steers every future self-review, and a phantom two-arg signature either gets cargo-culted or undermines trust in the override. Every other code anchor in the file checks out, which makes this one stand out.

```suggestion
  `safe_repo_path(candidate)`. Direct `Path.resolve()` on
```

## Verdict

Solid, well-documented dogfooding infrastructure whose code anchors almost all verify cleanly — but the new release step's placement can silently suppress GitHub Release publication, and the self-review wiring now hard-fails on any branch lacking the extension file. Three warnings worth addressing before merge.

## Findings

| # | Severity | File | Summary |
|---|----------|------|---------|
| 1 | ⚠️ warning | `.github/workflows/auto-release.yml:175` | Step 3.5 failure after tag push skips Steps 4–5 — tag public, GitHub Release never created, and a re-run self-heals green |
| 2 | ⚠️ warning | `.github/workflows/auto-release.yml:206` | Unpinned `npx --yes skills` runs `skills@latest` with a persisted push-to-main token in `.git/config` |
| 3 | ⚠️ warning | `.github/workflows/self-review.yml:232` | Missing `.review/extension.md` on stale branches / fork PRs hard-fails all review legs (`reviewer.py:3667`) |
| 4 | ℹ️ info | `.github/workflows/auto-release.yml:209` | `git diff --quiet` misses untracked new files; pure-addition releases silently no-op with a false "already at" message |
| 5 | ℹ️ info | `.agents/skills/ai-diff-reviewer/SKILL.md:360` | Duplicated "Option A" line, vendored from the released tag — fix belongs in `skills/` (source of truth) |
| 6 | ℹ️ info | `.review/extension.md:136` | `safe_repo_path(repo_root, candidate)` cites a two-arg signature; the real one takes a single arg |

## What I verified and found correct

The verification quality of this PR is genuinely high, and it shows:

- **Vendored-copy integrity.** `.agents/skills/ai-diff-reviewer/` is byte-identical to the `skills/ai-diff-reviewer/` source-of-truth, and the vendored `prompt.md` is byte-identical to `prompts/default.md` — the two-copy invariant this PR formalizes starts out actually true.
